features: Understands your codebase, edits files and runs commands
claude-code.pricing_summary: Included with Claude paid plans; Pro is $17/mo billed annually ($20 monthly), with higher tiers above.
claude-code.free_plan: Claude has a free plan for chat; Claude Code itself is tied to paid plans (check pricing page).
pros: Handles multi-file changes and long tasks well
Works directly in your terminal and repo
cons: Needs a paid Claude plan
CLI-first workflow is less friendly for non-developers

features: Agents that turn ideas into code
Tab completion and chat in a VS Code-style editor
Cloud agents and automations on higher plans
cursor.pricing_summary: Free plan, then paid individual plans (listed from $8/mo up to $200/mo) plus team plans; third-party models billed by usage on some plans.
cursor.free_plan: Yes: free plan with limited agent and chat requests.
pros: Strong agent mode and tab completion
cons: Usage limits differ a lot between plans
Third-party model usage can be billed separately

features: Works in your editor, terminal, desktop and on GitHub
Agent mode, code review and Copilot cloud agent
Usage measured in GitHub AI Credits
github-copilot.free_plan: Yes: Free plan with limited chat and agent usage (supports CLI and agent mode).
pros: Tight integration from issue to pull request on GitHub
cons: Credit-based usage can be hard to predict
Best experience assumes your code is on GitHub

features: Codex on web, CLI, IDE extension and iOS
Cloud integrations like automatic GitHub code review and Slack
API-key mode for CI and automation
AGENTS.md custom instructions, skills, MCP, subagents
openai-codex.pricing_summary: Included in ChatGPT plans: Free $0, Go $8/mo, Plus $20/mo, Pro from $100/mo; or pay API rates with an API key.
openai-codex.free_plan: Yes: limited Codex access on the ChatGPT Free plan (desktop app, subject to rollout).
pros: Included if you already pay for ChatGPT
Runs locally, in the cloud and in CI
cons: Usage allowance varies by model and task size
Cloud features are not available with API-key auth

features: Manage local and cloud agents from one surface
Unlimited Tab completions and inline edits
Access to frontier models plus SWE-2
windsurf.pricing_summary: Free $0; Pro $20/mo; Max $200/mo; Teams $80/mo + $40/mo per full dev seat; Enterprise custom.
windsurf.free_plan: Yes: Free plan with a light agent quota and unlimited Tab completions.
pros: Agentic IDE that is a solid Cursor alternative
cons: Free plan has limited model availability
Heavier agent use needs Pro or Max

features: Build websites and web apps by chatting
Add AI features to your apps
lovable.pricing_summary: Credit-based plans priced by included credits, not seats (Pro, Business, Enterprise); student discount available.
lovable.free_plan: Yes: 5 daily build credits (up to 30/month) plus 20 monthly Cloud credits.
pros: Very beginner-friendly; no technical knowledge needed
Unlimited workspace members on all plans
cons: Credit usage varies by task complexity
Monthly plan credits expire after two months

features: Build websites and apps from prompts
Custom domains and SEO boosting on Pro
bolt.pricing_summary: Free $0; Pro $25/mo; Teams $30/member/mo (save up to 28% yearly).
bolt.free_plan: Yes: 1M tokens/month (300K daily), hosting, Bolt branding on sites.
pros: Unused tokens roll over on Pro
cons: Free plan shows Bolt branding
Token limits can run out on bigger projects

features: Replit Agent builds apps from chat
Database rollback (up to 28 days on higher plan)
Collaboration with up to 15 collaborators on Pro
replit.pricing_summary: Core $20/mo ($18 annually) with $20 of model credit; Pro $100/mo ($90 annually) with $100 credit; Enterprise custom.
replit.free_plan: Yes: a free Starter tier (check pricing page for limits).
pros: All-in-one: code, agent, database and deploy
cons: Agent output can be inconsistent (Replit notes it is probabilistic)
Costs grow with heavier model usage

features: Design and build full-stack web apps with AI
v0.pricing_summary: Free $0; Plus $30/user/mo; Business $100/user/mo; Enterprise custom; extra credits purchasable.
v0.free_plan: Yes: free access with a 7 messages/day limit.
cons: Low daily message limit on free plan
Tied closely to the Vercel ecosystem

supabase.pricing_summary: Free $0; Pro from $25/mo; Team from $599/mo; Enterprise custom.
supabase.free_plan: Yes: 500 MB database, 50,000 MAU, 1 GB storage; 2 active projects; paused after 1 week inactivity.
pros: Default backend for many AI app builders
cons: Free projects pause when inactive
Usage-based overages on Pro

features: Analytics, Crashlytics, Remote Config, Firebase AI Logic
firebase.pricing_summary: Spark plan is no-cost; Blaze is pay-as-you-go (eligible users can get $300 free credit).
firebase.free_plan: Yes: Spark plan with no-cost usage limits, no payment method needed.
pros: Broad Google-backed platform for mobile and web
Many products free at small scale
cons: NoSQL data model differs from SQL
Pay-as-you-go bills can be hard to predict

neon.pricing_summary: Free $0; Launch and Scale are usage-based (e.g. $0.106/CU-hr on Launch).
neon.free_plan: Yes: 100 projects, 100 CU-hours/month per project, 1 GB storage per project, no credit card.
pros: Scales to zero; pay per usage
cons: Usage-based billing needs monitoring
Free storage per project is small

features: File storage, text and vector search
convex.pricing_summary: Free & Starter $0 + pay as you go; Professional $25/developer/mo; Business from $2,500/mo minimum.
convex.free_plan: Yes: Free & Starter plan for 1–6 developers.
pros: Reactive, real-time data out of the box
cons: Proprietary platform rather than plain SQL
Business tier has a high monthly minimum

features: Web Application Firewall and DDoS mitigation
vercel.pricing_summary: Hobby $0; Pro $20/mo with $20 included usage credit; Enterprise custom.
vercel.free_plan: Yes: Hobby plan for personal projects.
cons: Usage costs can climb at scale
Hobby plan is for non-commercial/personal use

features: Deploy from AI, Git or API
Functions, Netlify Database and Blob storage
Firewall traffic rules and global CDN
netlify.pricing_summary: Free $0; Personal $9/mo; Pro $20/mo (unlimited members, credit tiers); Enterprise custom.
netlify.free_plan: Yes: free forever plan with 300 credits/month.
cons: Credit-based limits to keep an eye on
Advanced analytics need paid plans

features: Pages Functions billed as Workers requests
cloudflare-pages.pricing_summary: Static requests free on all plans; Functions use Workers Free or Workers Paid quotas.
cloudflare-pages.free_plan: Yes: unlimited static requests; Functions share the Workers Free 100,000 requests/day limit.
cons: Functions limits shared with Workers
Fewer framework conveniences than Vercel

features: Deploy web services, workers and databases
Custom domains, firewall and DDoS mitigation
Previews and horizontal autoscaling on Pro
render.pricing_summary: Hobby $0 + compute; Pro $25/mo + compute; Scale $499/mo + compute; Enterprise custom.
render.free_plan: Yes: Hobby plan (up to 25 services, 5 GB bandwidth) plus compute costs.
pros: Good for background workers and APIs
cons: Compute billed on top of plan fee
Advanced governance needs Scale plan

features: Broad model lineup via one API
Large ecosystem of SDKs and tools
openai-api.pricing_summary: Pay per token; rates vary by model (see official pricing).
openai-api.free_plan: No ongoing free tier listed; pay as you go.
cons: Costs scale with tokens
Model lineup changes often

features: Managed agent harness and context management
Infrastructure for running agents in production
anthropic-api.pricing_summary: Pay per token; rates vary by model (see API tab on the pricing page).
anthropic-api.free_plan: No ongoing free tier listed; pay as you go.
pros: Strong for coding and long-context work
cons: Costs scale with tokens
Fewer modalities than some rivals

features: Context caching and Batch API (50% cost reduction) on paid tier
google-gemini-api.pricing_summary: Free tier, then paid per-token tier with higher rate limits; Enterprise available.
google-gemini-api.free_plan: Yes: free input and output tokens on limited models (free-tier content is used to improve Google products).
cons: Free tier data may be used to improve products
Free tier has limited model access

features: One API for many models and providers
openrouter.pricing_summary: Free plan, then Standard/Business/Enterprise; pay per token by model.
openrouter.free_plan: Yes: 25+ free models across 4 free providers.
cons: Adds a middle layer between you and providers
Budgets and prompt caching need paid tiers

groq.pricing_summary: Free tier, then pay per token (see official pricing).
groq.free_plan: Yes: free tier available (check rate limits).
cons: Model choice limited to what Groq hosts
Free tier rate limits

openai-agents-sdk.pricing_summary: Free and open source; you pay for model usage.
cons: Best fit with OpenAI models
Less batteries-included than bigger frameworks

langgraph.pricing_summary: Open-source library; LangSmith platform: Developer $0/seat, Plus $39/seat/mo, Enterprise custom, plus pay as you go.
langgraph.free_plan: Yes: open source; Developer plan with up to 5k base traces/month.
cons: Steeper learning curve
Platform costs scale with traces and seats

features: Unified TypeScript SDK for many model providers
vercel-ai-sdk.pricing_summary: Free and open source; you pay for model usage.
cons: TypeScript only
Hosting and model costs are separate

features: Deploy on CrewAI cloud, your VPC or own infra (Enterprise)
crewai.free_plan: Yes: Basic plan with 50 workflow executions/month; open-source framework.
cons: Free plan executions are limited
Enterprise pricing not public

features: Workflow automation with AI agents, MCP and AI nodes
n8n.pricing_summary: Self-host community edition free; Cloud Starter €20/mo and Pro €50/mo billed annually; Business/Enterprise above.
n8n.free_plan: Self-hosting is free; Cloud plans come with a free trial (no credit card).
cons: Cloud plans priced by executions
Self-hosting needs maintenance

features: AI video and image generation (Gen-4.5, Gen-4 Turbo)
Music, voice and sound effects generation
4K upscaling, no watermarks on paid plans
runway.pricing_summary: Free $0 (125 one-time credits); Standard $12/mo annually; Pro $28/mo annually; Team & Enterprise available.
pros: Many top video models in one place
cons: Credits get used up quickly on video
Free credits are one-time only

features: AI creative studio for cinematic video
google-veo-flow.pricing_summary: See official site; availability and pricing depend on your Google plan.
pros: Access to Google's Veo video models
cons: Pricing and availability vary by plan and region

kling-ai.pricing_summary: Free credits, then paid plans (see official site).
cons: Credit-based pricing
Pricing details are not on the homepage

features: AI avatar videos with your face and voice
175+ languages and voice cloning on paid plans

heygen.free_plan: Yes: 3 videos/month, up to 1 minute each.
cons: Free videos are short and limited
Higher quality exports need paid plans

features: Text to speech and speech to text
elevenlabs.pricing_summary: Free $0; Starter $6/mo; Creator $22/mo; Pro $99/mo; Scale $299/mo; Business $990/mo.
pros: Wide range of audio tools and APIs
cons: Commercial license needs a paid plan
Credits run out fast for long audio

openai-realtime-api.pricing_summary: Pay per use; rates vary by model (see official pricing).
pros: Same platform as other OpenAI APIs
cons: Can be costly for long calls
Requires handling realtime connections

Choose transcriber, model and voice providers
